posts.title: Why we log every room every 10 minutes
posts.excerpt: Every numbered room at Koori is read every ten minutes, and the customer is called within fifteen minutes if the room leaves its band.
posts.content:
Koori Cold Stores gives a shipper a numbered room in a temperature band and holds it there. The log is how that work is checked. There are twelve rooms and 6,400 pallet positions at Quay 3, 18 Saltmarsh Road, Northmere Port. Readings are taken every ten minutes, twenty-four hours a day. Once a week the customer receives the log as a PDF and as a CSV. The file is included in the storage rate. It is not a separate charge.

The dock opens at 05:00. At 06:00 the log for all twelve rooms is reviewed. A sample from one morning shows the shape of that review. At 06:00, Room 7, frozen, read −20.6 °C and was in band. At 06:10, Room 11, deep frozen, read −26.1 °C and was in band. At 06:20, Room 2, chilled, read +3.2 °C and was in band. Those three lines are three steps of the same ten-minute pattern. The gap between them is the gap we publish.

The bands are fixed, and the log uses those bands as its marks. Chilled is +2 to +4 °C, rooms 1 to 5, with 2,600 positions, for dairy, fresh produce and chilled ready meals. Koori does not run a ripening band, so bananas and tropical fruit are not taken there. Frozen is −18 to −21 °C, rooms 6 to 10, with 2,900 positions, for frozen vegetables, bakery dough and ready meals. Deep frozen is −25 to −28 °C, rooms 11 and 12, with 900 positions, for fish, seafood and ice cream. Room 7 at −20.6 °C sits inside −18 to −21 °C. Room 11 at −26.1 °C sits inside −25 to −28 °C. Room 2 at +3.2 °C sits inside +2 to +4 °C. The line on the log says in band. The target written down is the band itself.

A reading starts at the door. When the first pallet of a booking comes in, Samuel Okafor, the dock supervisor, takes a probe reading at the dock seal and logs it with the room number. The seal is one of eight seals on the dock. From that first reading, the room is on the ten-minute cycle. If a room leaves its band, the customer gets a call within fifteen minutes. Ten minutes is how often we look. Fifteen minutes is how soon we call.

The rest of the day keeps the same record in view. At 10:30 Henrik Valo, the refrigeration engineer, checks the plant: compressors, condensers, and the frost on the pipes. The plant has been ammonia and carbon dioxide since the rebuild in 2009, when rooms 6 to 12 were added. Morning enquiries are answered before 12:00. Lucía Ferraz calls back every enquiry that came in before noon, with a room number. Afternoon enquiries are answered by 17:00. At 20:30 Dev Raman, the night shift lead, walks every room with a torch and signs the night log. Aiyana Brooks looks after temperature records and quality, which is where the weekly PDF and CSV are kept in order. Those jobs read the record the probes are already writing.

The store has kept a numbered room at the centre of the work for a long time. Jonas Ekdahl founded Koori in 1987 with two rooms on Quay 3. Marit Ekdahl has run it since 2016. The room count now is twelve. The log runs on every shift. Dock hours are Monday to Friday, 05:00 to 21:00, and Saturday, 06:00 to 14:00. Sunday and public holidays the doors are closed, unless an after-hours slot has been booked at €45.00 for 30 minutes. Readings continue every ten minutes through a closed day.

The night walk and the ten-minute reading do different work. The walk is a check a person signs at 20:30. The reading is the record between walks. Room 7 at 06:00 and the next line for Room 7 are not the same line. We publish the band, the interval, and the call within fifteen minutes if the room leaves the band.

The booking steps end where the log begins. You ask, and we acknowledge the same day. Within one working day you receive a room offer: room number, positions, start date and rate, held for 48 hours. When you confirm, you sign the storage order and book the first 30-minute dock slot. When the first pallet comes in, the probe at the seal starts the log. Weekly storage, before VAT, is €9.40 chilled, €11.20 frozen and €13.80 deep frozen. Handling in and handling out are €6.50 per pallet each. The weekly file travels with that booking.

If you want a room, start with a capacity enquiry. The office phone is 010 377 4120, Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00. Written notes go to ask@koori-coldstore.example. We reply within one working day. Room alerts are the separate list: one short email when a room in your band frees up, at most twice a month, and nothing else.

posts.title: What a 48-hour room offer means
posts.excerpt: A room offer names the room, the positions, the start date and the rate, and it is held for 48 hours.
posts.content:
Within one working day of an enquiry, Lucía Ferraz sends a room offer: the room number, the positions, the start date and the rate. The offer is held for 48 hours, which gives you time to sign the storage order and to book the first 30-minute dock slot.

If the 48 hours pass, the room goes back on the register. Nothing is charged for an offer that is not confirmed.

posts.title: Room 12 is back in the deep-frozen band
posts.excerpt: Room 12 has returned to service at −25 to −28 °C after its scheduled coil defrost.
posts.content:
Room 12 returned to service this week after its scheduled coil defrost. It holds the deep-frozen band, −25 to −28 °C, together with Room 11, which gives 900 positions for fish, seafood and ice cream.

Henrik Valo checked the plant on the morning of the return, and Aiyana Brooks confirmed the first full day of readings in the log before any pallet was put away.
